title: Hanoi-Style Turmeric Fish with Dill, Spring Onions and Rice Noodles
summary: Golden turmeric-marinated fish is seared until crisp, then tossed with wilted dill and spring onion and served over rice noodles with herbs, peanuts and a sweet-sour dipping sauce.
equipment: large non-stick or well-seasoned frying pan (30 cm)

ingredients.item: firm skinless white fish fillets (monkfish, cod or hake), cut into 4 cm pieces
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
fresh dill, thick stalks removed, fronds in 4 cm sprigs

steps.title: Marinate the Fish
steps.text: Blend the turmeric, ginger, shallots, garlic, fish sauce, sugar and 1 tablespoon of oil into a smooth paste. Wearing gloves or using a food bag over your hand, since turmeric stains skin and work surfaces, rub the paste all over the fish pieces, then cover and chill for 30 minutes-2 hours. This gives the turmeric time to colour the fish and the aromatics time to season it right through.

steps.title: Make the Dipping Sauce
steps.text: Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and warm water together until the sugar fully dissolves, then stir in the garlic and chilli. Divide among four small bowls; using warm water helps dissolve the sugar evenly so the sauce isn't gritty, and letting it sit mellows the sharp lime.

steps.title: Cook the Noodles
steps.text: Cook the rice vermicelli in a large pan of boiling unsalted water as the packet directs, usually 3-5 minutes, until just tender. Drain and rinse under cold water, shaking off the excess, which washes away surface starch so the strands stay separate rather than clumping. Divide among four bowls.

steps.title: Sear the Fish
steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of the cooking oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering, then lay the fish in one layer with space between the pieces, frying in two batches if needed. Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until golden underneath, turn carefully and cook a further 2-3 minutes until the fish is opaque all the way through and flakes when pressed, reaching at least 63°C in the centre of the thickest piece. Leaving the fish alone while it sears lets a proper golden crust form instead of steaming in its own moisture.

steps.title: Wilt the Herbs
steps.text: Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the same pan, then tip in the spring onions and dill and toss for 30-60 seconds until bright green and just wilted. Return the fish and its juices, turning gently once to coat, then take the pan off the heat straight away so the dill stays fresh rather than turning dull from overcooking.

steps.title: Assemble and Serve
steps.text: Spoon the fish, wilted herbs and pan oil over the bowls of noodles, then scatter with mint, coriander and chopped peanuts. Let everyone spoon over dipping sauce to taste, stirring it through just before eating so the noodles soak up its sweet-sour tang.

tips: Wear gloves when handling the turmeric paste — it stains skin and worktops and is hard to scrub off.
A common mistake is crowding the fish in the pan, which steams rather than sears it; fry in batches so each piece gets a proper golden crust.
Rinse the noodles in cold, not hot, water — cold water stops them cooking further and keeps the strands from turning gluey.
Add the dill right at the end and take the pan off the heat quickly, as long cooking dulls both its colour and flavour.
storage: Keep the fish, noodles and herbs separately in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat the fish gently until piping hot (74°C) before combining, rather than reheating the noodles and herbs, which are best eaten fresh. The dipping sauce keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
